title: Bioterrorism

source.boundary: Actual Chapter9 Bioterrorism title lower right PDF23/printed41 through references at bottom left PDF29/printed47. Actual Chapter10 Radiation Injuries title starts at top right PDF29/printed47. Reading order follows columns, not the running headers. Chapter8 material above the opening title and in the left column of PDF23, and Chapter10 material in the right column of PDF29, are excluded.
source.verification: Worker checked source and rendered boundaries; main independently verified all16 term/page occurrences and inspected the shared boundary pages. Vocabulary presence only, not clinical recommendations, current practice or mnemonic effectiveness.

scope: Sixteen selected terms, not exhaustive chapter coverage or a quota. Offline vocabulary candidates only, not clinical teaching, medical anchors, narration or image-generation prompts. New proposals are independently composed generic designs, not copied proprietary scenes; originality against all existing mnemonics is unverified.

entries.cue: Recognizable ant carrying a small coat rack.
entries.cue_scope: Ant plus rack as an approximate learned anthrax name bridge
entries.reason: Independently proposed familiar object pair, not a proprietary character or scene. Ant-rack is approximate and does not encode every sound; rack naming and learned recovery are untested. Not organism appearance, exposure, symptoms or a claim about insects carrying disease.

entries.cue: Miniature fox beside a much larger ordinary fox.
entries.reason: Familiar size contrast and compact near-sound phrase; fox/pox changes a consonant and requires learning. Not a clinical rash representation, animal reservoir or transmission claim. A small fox need not uniquely identify the disease without lesson context.

entries.cue: Recognizable wooden award plaque with a raised trophy emblem and no writing.
entries.reason: A familiar nameable object gives a compact learned association. Final k/g voicing differs; trophy or sign naming and dental-plaque collisions remain untested. Name only, not etiology, subtype, clinical finding or a treatment cue.

entries.cue: Oversized empty glass bottle with an unmistakable neck and stopper.
entries.cue_scope: Bottle as a partial learned botul- name cue
entries.reason: Bottle supplies a familiar approximate partial name, not an exact full-word rebus. Recognition and pronunciation need testing; retain under the user's learned-partial standard rather than adding forced syllables. No food contents, toxin source, exposure route or mechanism is asserted.

No economical association proposed in this pass. No syllable pile or unsourced disease-to-animal link added. This is not a requirement for full-syllable encoding or proof that a useful partial cue cannot exist.

entries.cue: Pool cue leaning beside a thermometer with a conspicuously high column.
entries.reason: Cue gives the letter-name homophone without written Q; thermometer is a familiar category prop, not a measurement or diagnostic threshold. Separate composition from the rejected beaver/fever proposal in docs/sound-bridge-workshop.json; that rejected design is not reused or promoted.

entries.cue: Rice visibly IN a clear container.
entries.reason: Reuse existing candidate with its visible in relationship and untested pronunciation. Not a claim that rice contains or produces ricin; no toxicology or preparation instructions. This chapter match is Table9-1, not adjacent Chapter8 prose.

entries.cue: Oversized wristwatch whose face contains a simple cartoon microbe token instead of numerals.
entries.reason: Familiar watch with a learned biology token makes a short name composition. Not a real sensor, program logo, pathogen depiction, sampling method or capability claim.

entries.cue: Large binoculars overlooking a miniature town of homes and a clinic.
entries.reason: Ordinary watchfulness and community setting support a learned category association. Not literal observation of individual patients, a data-collection protocol, surveillance technology or evidence of detection performance.

entries.cue: Egg in a recognizable incubator beside an unmarked hourglass.
entries.prior: New composition using duration-hourglass primitive in docs/visual-cue-catalog.json.
entries.reason: Familiar incubation setting with an existing duration primitive. No numerical interval, temperature, microbial growth model or clinical timing claim; egg is wordplay, not a pathogen source.

entries.cue: Single study mannequin on a small island separated by water from a group on the shore.
entries.reason: Familiar separation scene supports the word without requiring equipment-specific recognition. Not abandonment, physical restraint, an isolation-room design, mode of precautions or operational advice.

entries.cue: Shower removing conspicuous surface stains from a protective-suit mannequin.
entries.reason: Preserves existing familiar cleaning/removal cue. Not a universally applicable procedure, fluid, duration, chemical-specific method or protection recommendation.

entries.cue: Additional open care spaces facing a wave of arrivals.
entries.reason: Reuse established surge capacity cue for the source's longer phrase; also reused in Chapters5/6. Visible extra room, not crowd alone, carries capacity. Does not encode surge capability, staffing, numerical capacity or response procedures.

entries.cue: Two distinct ambulance teams each helping the other, each supporting the other's equipment.
entries.reason: Preserves earlier reciprocal-help design rather than inventing a second mapping. Mutuality must remain visible; ordinary teamwork is a plausible collision, not a reason to demand unique recognition. No administrative agreement or operational rule encoded.

entries.cue: Warehouse shelves holding a large orderly reserve of closed supply crates.
entries.cue_scope: Reserve stockpile category; official-name modifiers supplied by lesson context
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; related but distinct from push-packs in docs/chapter-5-cue-audit.json
entries.reason: Familiar stored reserve supports the stockpile headword without forcing Strategic or National into extra objects. Generic warehouse, not official branding, inventory, access or distribution instructions. Distinct from existing pushing-cart/push-packs action; recognition and discrimination untested.

Previously rejected docks plus bicycle assembly is not revived or silently reclassified as reuse. No improved economical partial association proposed in this pass. Broad calibration permits partial cues, but does not obligate retaining this particular attempt. No treatment association admitted.
